cohort: The study included 28,314 delivery cases from the Xi County New Cooperative Medical Scheme (NCMS) agency across two periods: 2009-2010 and 2014-2015.
finding: The Case Payment Reform (CPR) in Xi County failed to control the increase in caesarean section (CS) rates and total delivery medical costs, which continued to rise after its implementation.
mod_finding: After the CPR, CS rates increased from 26.1% to 32.5%, and both the length of stay and total medical cost significantly increased for both CS and vaginal delivery groups.
